newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SPT RISES IN FT EUROPE 500, CEZ DROPS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SPT RISES IN FT EUROPE 500, CEZ DROPS.

text.p: Czech fixed-line telephone monopoly SPT Telecom a.s. has moved up to become the 303rd largest European company by market capitalisation, according to the Financial Times 500 list published on Friday.
SPT, with $2.9 billion in market capitalisation at the end of 1996 according to the Financial Times, moved up from 332nd place in the 1995 FT Europe 500.
The main Czech power producer and distrubutor CEZ a.s. fell to 401st rank, with market cap of $2.04 billion, down from 335th position in the previous year.
The largest Czech commerical bank, Komercni Banka a.s., entered the list for the first time at 450th position, at $1.7 billion.

Royal Dutch/Shell was once again the largest European Company in the FT list with market cap of $135 billion, followed by Roche Holding of Switzerland ($72 billion), and British Petroleum ($58 billion).

No Slovak companies were on the FT Europe 500 list, and none of the Czech companies made it to the FT's Global 500 list where U.S. General Electric Co. moved up to first position from second last year with market cap of $150 billion, followed by Royal Dutch/Shell, and the Coca-Cola Corp ($126.8 billion).
Japan's Nippon Telegraph & Telephone fell from first to fourth on the global list.
Of the top ten on the FT Europe 500 1996 list, three companies were Swiss, three British, two Dutch-Anglo, one Italian, and one German.
On the FT Global 500, six were U.S.-based companies, three Japanese, and one Dutch-Anglo.
